headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Notion AI’s shared workspace access plus vendor egress can expose content if paired with a content-writing agent that feeds untrusted outputs into workspace workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection path is not documented, but B’s shared workspace state and page/database surfaces mean A’s content could be copied into Notion workflows manually or by the user. A is content-writing and B is workspace Q&A, so prompt-like text can be reinterpreted if bridged. This is lower severity because no automatic shared channel is shown.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into a Notion page that B later summarizes or answers from, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is configured to treat page text as authoritative instructions, malicious markup in A output can influence responses.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of shared Notion pages unless reviewed.
Prefix imported text as untrusted quotes.
Use a separate staging page for A drafts.
Disable any automation that republishes A output into B-readable pages.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to workspace content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read workspace pages and send content to vendor backends, while A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent that may generate or relay sensitive text. The pair creates a plausible leakage path through shared workspace content and external inference calls. This is medium because the workspace is the shared boundary, but no PHI or secret class is explicitly shown.
conditions: IF sensitive material is placed in pages accessible to B, B may transmit it to vendor backends.
IF A writes sensitive text into shared workspace content, B can ingest it from the same workspace.
mitigations: Restrict sensitive pages from B’s workspace scope.
Avoid placing secrets in A-generated drafts.
Review Notion AI usage on sensitive databases.
Use redacted copies for AI-assisted editing.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes broad network egress, while B has vendor-only egress and no filesystem, shell, or git write capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable local resource shown, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because B’s concurrency model mentions shared workspace state, but A has no write surface documented.
conditions: IF A and B are both given write access to the same external workspace through an undocumented integration, conflicts could arise.
IF the operator maps A output into a shared mutable page that B edits concurrently, last-write-wins collisions are possible.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits on the same page.
Use one agent as read-only reviewer.
Serialize edits through a human checkpoint.
Lock shared pages during AI-assisted updates.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking to shared workspace flows.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat A-produced text as source material if the operator places it in Notion. A is a content-writing agent, making it plausible that generated claims flow into B without verification. This is medium because the cascade exists in default workspace usage, though not automatically between the two agents.
conditions: IF A-generated claims are pasted into a Notion page, B may answer from them as if they were factual.
IF B is used to summarize A output without a verification step, errors can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require source links before B may reuse A claims.
Mark A drafts as unverified.
Add a human review step before publishing.
Use B only on curated pages.
requires-engineering: implement citation validation for workspace Q&A.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles workspace pages and team knowledge base content under Notion workspace permissions, while A is an open-source content-writing agent with broad network egress. If regulated data is stored in the workspace, B’s vendor-hosted processing can create residency or retention mismatches. A is not itself a residency-bound system, so the compliance risk centers on B.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated content is stored in pages accessible to B, vendor processing may create a residency or DPA mismatch.
IF retention policies differ between the workspace and vendor backends, compliance obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AI-enabled pages.
Confirm a DPA before using B on sensitive content.
Limit B to non-regulated workspaces.
Review retention settings.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated and unregulated workspaces.
